# Vendored third-party assets

Files here are **not ours**. They are copied verbatim from upstream so the editor
can render a reference diagram with no network access, and so the version it
compares against is pinned and explicit rather than whatever a CDN serves today.

## `mermaid/`

| | |
|---|---|
| Upstream | <https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid> |
| Package | `mermaid` on npm |
| Version | see `mermaid/.version` (currently **12.0.0**) |
| Licence | MIT — see `mermaid/LICENSE` |
| Copyright | 2014–2022 Knut Sveidqvist |

`mermaid.min.js` is the self-contained UMD bundle. It is the *smallest* offline
option: the ESM entry point is only 29 KB but dynamically imports the rest of the
12.8 MB `dist` tree, which would be far worse to ship.

**The minified bundle carries no licence banner** — esbuild strips it. MIT
requires the copyright and permission notice to travel with "all copies or
substantial portions", so `LICENSE` sits beside it and is embedded into the
assembly alongside the script. Do not remove it.

### Refreshing

```bash
cd oracle && npm ci
pwsh ../scripts/vendor-mermaid.ps1
```

Pin deliberately. This bundle is the reference the comparison pane renders
against, so bumping it changes what "correct" looks like — re-run the oracle
after any bump.

The reference shell explicitly keeps `layout: dagre`, `theme: default` (or the
selected dark theme) and `look: classic` so Mermaid 12's new defaults do not
silently change existing previews. Authored frontmatter overrides remain authored.
Bundled ELK is not a reinstatement of the removed native-editor layout commands.
The standalone comparison generator now uses bundled dagre/ELK; its old
Mermaid-11-only tidy-tree dependency is not installed into the Mermaid 12 oracle.

## Why vendor at all

Three reasons, in order of importance:

1. **Offline.** Previewing a diagram must not require a network round trip.
2. **Determinism.** A pinned bundle means a rendering difference is a real
   difference, not a silent upstream release.
3. **No CSP or CDN failure modes** inside the webview.

## `zenuml/`

The validation page separately embeds the standalone `@zenuml/core` **3.47.9**
UMD bundle, copied verbatim from the installed oracle dependency. Its source is
<https://github.com/mermaid-js/zenuml-core/tree/e3f93e0eb65d23fa3520e8691a5bca883853aa4b>.
It is MIT licensed, copyright 2022 Peng Xiao; its `LICENSE` and collected
production-dependency notices travel with the asset and the package.

Refresh with `pwsh scripts/vendor-zenuml.ps1` after installing the pinned oracle
dependencies. The refresh refuses a changed version or a script-closing token
that would make inline embedding unsafe. Dependency notices are regenerated by
`scripts/zenuml-license-notices.mjs`. ANTLR's installed 4.11.0 package omits its
license file: `upstream-notices/antlr4-4.11.0-LICENSE.txt` is the exact upstream
<https://github.com/antlr/antlr4/blob/4.11.0/LICENSE.txt>, Git blob
`5d276941558adc380d467a0a34ae92bbeb6e4fec`. The `dlv` publisher's license reference
is recorded explicitly because its release and npm package have no license file.

This is not the published `@mermaid-js/mermaid-zenuml` adapter: that adapter's
parser does nothing and cannot establish syntax validity. Our small, separate
validation adapter awaits the public standalone parser and rejects its reported
errors. The upstream bundle itself is not patched. Reference preview rendering
and native editing support are separate from this grammar integration.
